messages:
alex: Hey folks, ran into a weird billing situation. Booked conference travel to Copenhagen via an OTA package (flight+hotel) and the vendor charged one lump sum. Hotel later posted a separate "resort/service fee" and a city tax on checkout. I shared an airport Uber with a colleague (split in the app) but our drop-offs diverged so app shows two legs under one receipt. Can I expense the hotel nights for the conference only and my share of the Uber? Also the OTA shows only a single charge on my corporate cardcc @ashley @travel-ops

ashley: Short answers: (1) Lodging for business nights is reimbursable. (2) Shared ground transport that was business-related is reimbursable for your portion. (3) OTA lump sums complicate itemization but we have a workflow.

travel-ops: Workflow: ask the OTA for an itemized invoice breaking out flight vs hotel. If they can't provide it, request a hotel folio from the property showing nightly rates and taxes. If neither party can itemize, create an attestation explaining the split and attach the conference invite.

tom: For the Uber: the app receipt with split amounts is ideal. If the app shows a single trip with two drop-off legs, screenshot the trip map and payment breakdown. Finance can accept the in-app split or a signed attestation from the colleague confirming the split.

alex: The OTA says they won't issue an itemized invoice (only a single booking reference). Hotel says they can provide folio but it will only show total charged to the OTA. Ugh.

finance-bot: Policy excerpt: "Expenses must be substantiated with vendor receipts. When vendor invoicing aggregates charges, employees should obtain any available vendor folios or provide a brief attestation describing the breakdown and attach supporting proof (conference registration, calendar invite). Manager approval is required for attested itemization."

travel-ops: Practical steps for you: 1) Request hotel folio and OTA booking confirmation (push for any nightly detail). 2) In Expensify: create two expenses: 'Lodging - business nights' (attach conference invite + folio or attestation) and 'Personal/OTA remainder' (mark personal). 3) For the Uber: attach the app receipt screenshot and include the colleague's name; if split shows in app, claim your portion. If not, add colleague attestation and tag me for quick verification.

alex: What about the resort/service fee? The folio flags it as "mandatory amenity fee" but it looks optional (pool access). Company policy reimburses mandatory taxes/fees but not optional amenities, right?

ashley: Correct: mandatory city taxes and compulsory lodging fees are reimbursable. Discretionary resort charges (spa, recreational packages) are not. If the folio labels it mandatory, we usually treat it as part of lodging; otherwise, exclude it. Add a note indicating the label on the folio.

alex: And the OTA charged a foreign currency conversion fee on my corporate card for the whole package. Can that FX fee be reimbursed if it's a company-paid travel?

finance-bot: If the corporate card was used for an eligible business expense, bank/merchant conversion fees are reimbursable. Attach the card statement showing the fee line and the OTA receipt.

alex: One last oddball: I rented an e-bike to get from hotel to venue (10min ride). Is micro-mobility reimbursable? No receipt other than app charge.

travel-ops: Micro-mobility (bike/scooter) is reimbursable when used as reasonable local transport for business legs. App charge screenshot is fine. If used for personal sightseeing, mark personal.

ashley: TL;DR: gather hotel folio/OTA confirmation, screenshot Uber split, attach conference invite, split expenses in Expensify, and request manager approval with notes. If you want, ping me and I'll pre-approve the attestation so finance clears faster.

alex: Thanks y'all I'll pull the folio and upload everything now. Appreciate it! :thumbsup:
